title: MyChatApp · Production overview
description: End-to-end operations view of MyChatApp: alerts and SLOs, API, AI pipeline, cost, guardrails, ingestion, data stores, traces and the telemetry stack. Hover the (i) on any panel for what it means.

panels.title: Start here  ·  how to read this dashboard in 30 seconds

options.content:
**Read top to bottom: each section answers the next question an on-call engineer would ask.** Colours mean the same everywhere: **green** = healthy, **orange** = getting worse, **red** = act now. Every other colour just tells series apart. Hover the **(i)** on any panel for what it means.

| Section | The question it answers | Look at first | Healthy looks like |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Service status** | Is anything broken *right now*? | Alarm tiles, the live map, component lanes | No alarms, every box and lane green |
| **Golden signals** | How is the app doing in this time range? | Server errors, API latency, Full answer | 0 errors, API under 0.5 s |
| **SLOs & error budget** | Are we keeping our promises to users? | The four dials | Dials in green, burn rate under 1× |
| **Traffic & errors** | Which endpoint is slow or failing? | Errors by route, Slowest routes | Only blue 401s, no red 5xx |
| **AI pipeline** | Where does an answer's time go? | Time per step, First word heatmap | Most time in *ollama /api/chat*, first word under 3 s |
| **Caching · Tokens & cost · Guardrails** | What does the AI cost, and is it being attacked? | Cost per answer, Poisoned chunks | Poisoned chunks = 0 |
| **Ingestion · Data stores** | Are uploads processed, and are the databases OK? | Ingest backlog, Connections used | Backlog near 0, connections under 70% |
| **Traces** | What happened inside one slow request? | Click a Trace ID | The longest bar is where the time went |

**Something red?** Check *Active alerts* → find the matching red band on the graphs → click **Open slow traces** on a latency panel. **Everything empty?** Nobody is using the app: start the synthetic users (`--profile demo up -d --no-deps loadgen`, see docs/observability.md).

panels.title: Critical alarms
panels.description: Critical alerts firing now (alerts.yml): error budget burning fast, a component down, a poisoned document. Each one is listed in 'Active alerts' to the right.

panels.title: Warnings
panels.description: Warning alerts firing now: slow first word, saturation, ingest failures, cache errors.

panels.title: Availability
panels.description: Share of requests that did NOT fail with a server error (5xx), health probes excluded. SLO: 99.9%.

panels.title: Error budget left
panels.description: The SLO allows 0.1% of requests to fail. This is how much of that allowance is left, measured over the selected range. Below 0% = the SLO is missed for this period.

panels.title: First word p95
panels.description: How long users wait before the answer starts appearing (95th percentile). The single most important number for how fast the chatbot feels.

panels.title: Components up
panels.description: Every target Prometheus scrapes (app pods, data stores, telemetry stack) answering right now. The lanes below show which one is not.

panels.title: Live system map  ·  requests flow left to right
panels.description: The whole system on one screen, refreshed every 10 s. Box tint: green = up, red = down (Ollama: a model call failed in the last 5 min). Blue arrows: user requests through the API; purple: the ingestion workers. Numbers: API p95 excluding chat, Ollama median generation speed, Qdrant search p95, PostgreSQL commits per second, MinIO storage used.

panels.title: Component health
panels.description: Red = down (or, for Ollama, which has no metrics endpoint: a model call failed in the last 5 min, seen in traces). 'Ingestion workers' turns red when ANY worker is down.

panels.title: Active alerts
panels.description: Alerts firing right now, from deploy/observability/alerts.yml. Descriptions: http://localhost:9090/alerts. Their start/end are drawn on every graph as red marks.

panels.title: Requests / min
panels.description: Average requests per minute over the selected range (health probes excluded).

panels.title: Server errors
panels.description: Number of 5xx responses. Anything above 0 is worth a look: open the Traces section below.

panels.title: API latency p95
panels.description: 95% of non-chat requests (login, history, documents...) were faster than this. Chat is left out: its duration is the whole generated answer.

panels.title: Full answer p95
panels.description: Time from question to the last word of the answer (95th percentile).

panels.title: Answers given
panels.description: Chat + agent answers completed in the selected range.

panels.title: Active users
panels.description: Users who got at least one model answer in the selected range (llm_usage table in PostgreSQL).

targets.rawSql: SELECT count(DISTINCT user_id) FROM llm_usage WHERE $__timeFilter(created_at)

panels.title: No matching document
panels.description: Questions where no document chunk passed MIN_SCORE, so the model answered without your documents. High = users ask about things not in the knowledge base, or retrieval is broken.

panels.title: Agent tool failures
panels.description: Share of agent tool calls that failed (unknown tool, tool error).

panels.title: Estimated cost
panels.description: Model cost at the configured per-token prices. Details in Tokens & cost.

panels.title: Documents indexed
panels.description: Documents the ingestion workers finished in the selected range.

panels.title: Documents failed
panels.description: Documents given up on (unreadable file, or every retry failed). See the Ingestion section.

panels.title: Ingest backlog
panels.description: Documents waiting for, or being processed by, a worker right now (PostgreSQL).

targets.rawSql: SELECT count(*) FROM documents WHERE status IN ('queued', 'processing')

panels.title: Responses by status
panels.description: 2xx = fine, 4xx = the client's mistake (not logged in, not found), 5xx = ours.

panels.title: Token mix
panels.description: Input = prompt, documents and history; output = generated. Input dominating = big prompts.

panels.title: Answer cache
panels.description: First questions answered from the semantic cache (hit) vs by the model (miss).

panels.title: SLOs & error budget  ·  targets from alerts.yml
Availability SLI
panels.description: Requests that were not a 5xx. Target 99.9%: green = met for the selected range.

panels.title: API latency SLI
panels.description: Non-chat requests that took under 1 s. Target 99%.

panels.title: First word SLI
panels.description: Answers whose first word arrived within 10 s. Target 95%.

panels.title: Burn rate (1 h)
panels.description: How fast the error budget is being spent over the last hour. 1x = exactly the budget over 30 days. 6x pages a warning, 14.4x is critical (2% of the monthly budget in one hour).

panels.title: Error budget burn rate
panels.description: Dashed lines: 6x (warning) and 14.4x (critical). An alert needs BOTH a long and a short window above the line, so a single bad minute does not page anyone.

defaults.noValue: No data in this time range

panels.title: SLIs over time
panels.description: Each line should stay at or above its target: availability 99.9%, API latency 99%, first word 95%.

defaults.noValue: No data in this time range

panels.title: Traffic & errors  ·  is the API healthy?
Requests / min by route
panels.description: Where the traffic goes. Use the Route filter at the top to focus on one endpoint.

defaults.noValue: No data in this time range

panels.title: Errors / min by route
panels.description: Red = server errors (our bug or a dependency down). Orange = client errors (bad input, not found). Blue = 401 not logged in, usually harmless (expired session).

defaults.noValue: No data in this time range

panels.title: Latency percentiles (all selected routes)
panels.description: p50: half of requests are faster. p99: only 1 in 100 is slower. A gap between p50 and p99 means a few users have a much worse experience.

defaults.noValue: No data in this time range

panels.title: Slowest routes (p95, selected range)
panels.description: Chat routes are naturally slow: they include the whole generated answer.

defaults.noValue: No data in this time range

panels.title: Request latency heatmap (non-chat)
panels.description: Each column is one minute; each cell counts requests in that latency bucket (brighter = more). A second bright band higher up = a group of slow requests the p95 line would smooth away.

panels.title: AI pipeline  ·  where does a chat answer's time go?
Time per step (p95), from traces
panels.description: Every step inside a request, slowest first: ollama POST /api/chat = generating the answer, ollama POST /api/embed = embedding the question, qdrant ... = vector search, SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE = PostgreSQL, rag.retrieve = embedding + search together.

defaults.noValue: No data in this time range

panels.title: Time to first word vs full answer
panels.description: First word = how long the user stares at an empty bubble. The gap to the full answer is the time spent streaming the text.

defaults.noValue: No data in this time range

panels.title: Time to first word heatmap
panels.description: How long each answer took to start, minute by minute. Bright cells at the top = users waiting.

panels.title: Full answer heatmap
panels.description: Time from question to the last word, for every answer.

panels.title: Answers / min
panels.description: Answers completed per minute: chat = normal answers, agent = agent mode.

defaults.noValue: No data in this time range

panels.title: Document search latency
panels.description: Embedding the question (Ollama) + vector search (Qdrant). Log scale: normal searches take ~100 ms, a cold embedding model several seconds. Dashed line: 1 s, above which a search is slow.

defaults.noValue: No data in this time range

panels.title: Answered without documents
panels.description: A sudden jump usually means the index is empty or the embedding model changed.

defaults.noValue: No data in this time range
No data in this time range

panels.title: Caching  ·  answers and embeddings the models did not have to compute
First questions answered from cache
panels.description: Share of first questions answered without retrieval or the chat model. Follow-up questions are never cached. Low is normal right after a document upload: every upload empties the cache.

panels.title: Embeddings from cache
panels.description: Texts whose vector came from memory or PostgreSQL instead of the embedding model.

panels.title: Cache errors
panels.description: Cache reads/writes that failed; requests went ahead without the cache. Errors in the semantic cache right after an upload mean it may not have been emptied: look for 'could not be cleared' in the logs.

defaults.noValue: No data in this time range

panels.title: Embeddings / min by source
panels.description: memory = this process already had it, database = another process or an earlier run computed it, miss = sent to the embedding model.

defaults.noValue: No data in this time range

panels.title: Tokens & cost  ·  what the model is used for, and what it would cost
Tokens used
panels.description: Input (prompt + documents + history) and output (generated) tokens, in the selected range.

panels.title: Estimated cost
panels.description: Tokens x the prices in LLM_PRICE_INPUT_PER_MTOK / LLM_PRICE_OUTPUT_PER_MTOK. Ollama itself is free: by default this is what the same traffic would cost on a small paid model.

panels.title: Cost per answer
panels.description: Average estimated cost of one chat or agent answer.

panels.title: Input tokens per answer
panels.description: Prompt size of an average answer: instructions + retrieved chunks + chat history. Large and growing = long chats or too many chunks; it drives both cost and time to first word.

panels.title: Output tokens per answer
panels.description: Length of an average answer.

panels.title: Generation speed
panels.description: Median tokens per second the model generates (reported by Ollama). Under ~5/s answers feel slow; a GPU gives 50+.

panels.title: Tokens / min
panels.description: Input = what we send (prompt, documents, history). Output = what the model writes.

defaults.noValue: No data in this time range

panels.title: Estimated cost / hour by feature
panels.description: chat = normal answers, agent = agent mode (several model calls per answer), title = chat titles.

defaults.noValue: No data in this time range

panels.title: Generation speed
panels.description: Tokens per second. A drop means the model server is overloaded or swapped to CPU.

defaults.noValue: No data in this time range

panels.title: Usage by user (selected range)
panels.description: From the llm_usage table in PostgreSQL: one row per model call, with the user who made it. Cost at the prices configured when each call was made.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT coalesce(u.username, '(deleted user)') AS "User",
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE l.endpoint IN ('chat', 'agent')) AS "Answers",
       sum(l.input_tokens) AS "Input tokens",
       sum(l.output_tokens) AS "Output tokens",
       sum(l.input_tokens + l.output_tokens) AS "Total tokens",
       sum(l.cost_usd) AS "Est. cost",
       max(l.created_at) AS "Last used"
FROM llm_usage l LEFT JOIN users u ON u.id = l.user_id
WHERE $__timeFilter(l.created_at)
GROUP BY u.username
ORDER BY "Total tokens" DESC
LIMIT 50

panels.title: Guardrails  ·  what was blocked, and why
Blocked
panels.description: Questions refused, document chunks dropped, tool results and answers withheld. Details (rule, file, user) are in the audit log: event=guardrail.blocked.

panels.title: Flagged (monitor mode)
panels.description: What would have been blocked with GUARDRAILS_MODE=enforce. Use it to check for false positives first.

panels.title: Poisoned document chunks
panels.description: Retrievals that dropped a chunk carrying instructions. Not zero = a file in the knowledge base contains a prompt injection: find it in the audit log (source=...) and delete it.

panels.title: Guard model errors
panels.description: Content checks skipped because GUARD_MODEL failed. The check fails open: those messages were not classified.

panels.title: Guardrail events / hour by check
panels.description: injection_input = the user's message, injection_document = a retrieved chunk, injection_tool = an agent tool result, prompt_leak = the answer repeated the system prompt, content_* = Llama Guard.

defaults.noValue: No data in this time range

panels.title: Document ingestion  ·  background workers and their queue
Queued
panels.description: Documents waiting for a worker (PostgreSQL, right now).

targets.rawSql: SELECT count(*) FROM documents WHERE status = 'queued'

panels.title: Processing
panels.description: Documents a worker has claimed and is chunking / embedding right now.

targets.rawSql: SELECT count(*) FROM documents WHERE status = 'processing'

panels.title: Stuck > 15 min
panels.description: Claimed by a worker more than 15 minutes ago and still not done: the worker probably died with it. It is handed to another worker once its claim expires.

targets.rawSql: SELECT count(*) FROM documents WHERE status = 'processing' AND claimed_at < now() - interval '15 minutes'

panels.title: Oldest wait
panels.description: How long the oldest queued document has been waiting. Growing steadily = not enough workers.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT coalesce(extract(epoch FROM now() - min(b.created_at)), 0)
FROM documents d JOIN ingest_batches b ON b.id = d.batch_id WHERE d.status = 'queued'

panels.title: Failed (all time)
panels.description: Documents left in 'failed'. The table below shows why; re-queue them once fixed.

targets.rawSql: SELECT count(*) FROM documents WHERE status = 'failed'

panels.title: Workers up
panels.description: Worker pods answering Prometheus. docker-compose and Kubernetes both run 3.

panels.title: Documents / min by outcome
panels.description: indexed = done. retry = a dependency hiccup, it will be tried again. failed = given up.

defaults.noValue: No data in this time range

panels.title: Time per document
panels.description: Download from MinIO + chunk + embed + store, for one document.

defaults.noValue: No data in this time range
No data in this time range

panels.title: Batches (unfinished, or created in the selected range)
panels.description: filling = the producer is still adding documents, open = sealed and being worked on, done = every document ready or failed.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT b.id AS "Batch", b.source AS "Source", b.status AS "Status",
       count(d.doc_id) AS "Documents",
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE d.status = 'ready') AS "Ready",
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE d.status IN ('queued', 'processing')) AS "Pending",
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE d.status = 'failed') AS "Failed",
       b.created_at AS "Created"
FROM ingest_batches b LEFT JOIN documents d ON d.batch_id = b.id
WHERE b.status <> 'done' OR $__timeFilter(b.created_at)
GROUP BY b.id ORDER BY b.id DESC LIMIT 20

panels.title: Recent failures
panels.description: The last error a worker recorded for each failed document.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT filename AS "File", attempts AS "Attempts", error AS "Last error"
FROM documents WHERE status = 'failed'
ORDER BY claimed_at DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 20

panels.title: Data stores & model server  ·  PostgreSQL, Qdrant, MinIO, Ollama
PostgreSQL
panels.description: postgres-exporter can connect and query. DOWN = login, chat history and usage all fail.

panels.title: Connections used
panels.description: Open connections vs max_connections. Near 100% new requests wait for or fail to get a connection.

panels.title: Cache hit ratio
panels.description: Reads served from PostgreSQL's memory instead of disk. Below ~99% the database needs more RAM.

panels.title: Longest transaction
panels.description: Age of the oldest open transaction. A long one holds locks and blocks vacuum.

panels.title: PostgreSQL transactions / s
panels.description: Rollbacks are normal for a failed request; a rising share means errors inside transactions.

defaults.noValue: No data in this time range
No data in this time range

panels.title: PostgreSQL connections by state
panels.description: 'idle in transaction' = a connection holding a transaction open without doing anything: a leak.

defaults.noValue: No data in this time range

panels.title: Qdrant
panels.description: Vector database. DOWN = no document search: answers come without your documents.

panels.title: Vectors stored
panels.description: Points (document chunks) across all collections.

panels.title: Search p95
panels.description: Qdrant's own time for a vector search (95th percentile), without network or embedding time.

panels.title: Qdrant errors
panels.description: 5xx responses from Qdrant's REST API.

panels.title: Optimizations running
panels.description: Background index rebuilds. Searches can be slower while they run (e.g. right after a large ingest).

panels.title: Qdrant requests / min by endpoint
panels.description: points/query = searches from chat, points (PUT) = chunks written by ingestion.

defaults.noValue: No data in this time range
No data in this time range

panels.title: MinIO
panels.description: Object storage for the original files. DOWN = uploads and ingestion fail; chat still works.

panels.title: Disk free
panels.description: Free space on MinIO's volume.

panels.title: Rejected requests
panels.description: S3 calls MinIO refused (bad credentials, clock skew, invalid request). Usually a wrong MINIO_* setting.

targets.expr: (sum(increase(minio_s3_requests_rejected_auth_total[$__range])) or vector(0)) + (sum(increase(minio_s3_requests_rejected_header_total[$__range])) or vector(0)) + (sum(increase(minio_s3_requests_rejected_invalid_total[$__range])) or vector(0)) + (sum(increase(minio_s3_requests_rejected_timestamp_total[$__range])) or vector(0))

defaults.noValue: No data in this time range

panels.description: Ollama has no metrics endpoint: these come from the traces of our calls to it (Tempo span metrics). /api/chat = answers, /api/embed = embeddings.

panels.description: Whole call, including streaming the answer. Compare with 'Generation speed' in Tokens & cost.

panels.description: Built from traces. Each circle is a service; arrows show calls with their rate and latency. Red ring = errors.

panels.description: Every label combination is one series held in memory. A sudden jump = a label with unbounded values (a user id, a raw path) was added to a metric.
